summary.name: Demoscene Graphics
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit provenance: a 1990s demoscene demo direction in the Digital and 3D Aesthetics category. Use one coherent retro theme such as plasma fields, tunnels, rotating geometry, or bitmap lettering. Tie sections to music and return to a shared motif. Do not stack every classic effect or switch algorithms without rhythm.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: intros, music-driven title sequences, event openers with a supplied track, credits, greetings scrollers, and retro brand messages. Inferred: suits music-led or retro-tech subjects. Less suited to calm explanatory content, which the motion-020 guidance also flags.
summary.limitations: Use at most one primary effect per section, changing only on verified events. Do not flash faster than three times per second. Bitmap glyphs must stay at integer scales with no smoothing or blur. Beat or music-sync claims need inspected audio; the source verifies no audio timing.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent; #171629 is an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas. Suggested, not approved: foreground #F3EACF, accents #906ECC, #D87589, #53ADBD, a violet-coral-cyan family with no gradient. Foreground on background is 14.774. Dark #171629 text on #D87589 (5.769) or #53ADBD (6.829) is a candidate pairing. #906ECC (4.469) is decorative only. Task-provided exact colors override these; recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Shared-time procedural shaders own section visuals, with palette uniforms limited to primary tokens. Optional references: motion-002 vortex passage for meaningful chapter travel; motion-037 and motion-038 for phrase or punctuation steps when those assets exist; motion-039 for one emblem burst; motion-040 for hard word-card cuts; motion-020 only for deliberate digital disruption. Motion-012, -014, and -015 are secondary options. Interactive output needs pause and reduced-motion modes.
summary.audio: The metadata supplies no audio track, so none is claimed. Inferred suggestion: rhythm-led music that times sections and effect changes, with genre, tempo, and instrumentation unspecified. A supplied track is optional and must be authorized. Voiceover is unspecified and should not compete with scroller text. Silent previews are acceptable. Motion references suggest restrained accents or silence.
summary.assetRequirements: No mandatory uploads. Procedural effects need only code and local shader resources. Bitmap lettering needs a locally loaded pixel font, which the source does not specify. Motion references need inspected scene assets: actual phrase glyphs, punctuation marks, or approved emblem geometry. Do not invent brand marks or copy. A music track is optional and must be authorized.
summary.combinations: Style-105 supplies section and beat timing, feeding a shared time uniform and section indices into GLSL plasma or tunnel effects; best for music-driven openers. Style-057 supplies bitmap lettering, scrollers, and greetings in #F3EACF, integer-scaled over the shader, with a DOM mirror for HTML accessibility. Demoscene Graphics alone works when one coherent effect and a soundtrack carry the piece.
summary.productionApproach: Default pipeline is HyperFrames: data-composition-id, clip timing, one paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, then check, snapshot, and render. Remotion is a conditional fallback only, with a recorded reason. Style renderer: WebGL2, GLSL, and Three.js for procedural effects. Motion engine: GLSL, one owner per property. chroma-js is optional for validation. Seed randomness and verify seeks, loop seams, and audio sync.
